cards.text: Joseph, a young Hebrew just pulled out of the dungeon, has told Pharaoh, king of Egypt, what his dreams mean: seven good years, then seven years of famine. Then Joseph laid out a plan to save food for the hard years. Pharaoh and ALL his officials are pleased, and friend, when a whole room of officials agrees on something, you know it's a good plan.

cards.question: Pharaoh asks his officials if they can find anyone like Joseph. What does Pharaoh say abides in Joseph?

cards.text: Then Pharaoh turns to Joseph: since God made all this known to him, no one is as discerning and wise as Joseph. A few verses ago this man was in a DUNGEON, and believe me, I know a thing or two about getting pulled out of the dark.

cards.question: Pharaoh puts Joseph in charge of his house, and all his people are to obey Joseph. Then Pharaoh tells him, “Only with regard to the ___ will I be greater than you.”
Pharaoh goes even bigger and places Joseph over all the land of Egypt.

cards.text: Then Pharaoh pulls the signet ring off his own finger and puts it on Joseph's. That's like your boss handing you his company card AND his password on the same day you got hired.

cards.question: Next, Pharaoh dresses Joseph for the job. What does Pharaoh clothe Joseph in?
Along with the ring and the linen, Pharaoh also puts a gold chain around Joseph's neck.

cards.text: Then Pharaoh has Joseph ride in his second chariot, with men calling out before him. Look at this, friend. The man's got his OWN hype crew.

cards.question: As Joseph rides in Pharaoh's second chariot, what are the men in front of him calling out?

cards.text: Then Pharaoh declares to Joseph, “I am Pharaoh, but without your permission, no one in all the land of Egypt shall lift his hand or foot.” Hand OR foot, friend, you can't even stretch in the morning without running it by Joseph.

cards.question: Pharaoh gives Joseph a new Egyptian name. What else does Pharaoh give Joseph?

cards.text: His new name is Zaphenath-paneah, and his wife is Asenath, daughter of Potiphera, priest of On. Zaphenath-paneah... friend, I can't say that ONCE, and I've got nothing but time on this planet.

cards.question: Joseph is ___ years old when he enters the service of Pharaoh, king of Egypt.

cards.text: Joseph takes charge of all the land of Egypt, and he leaves Pharaoh's presence to travel throughout it. No corner office for this man; first day on the job and he's already out on the road.
The seven years of abundance arrive, and the land brings forth bountifully. Year after year after YEAR, those fields just keep showing out.

cards.question: During the seven good years, Joseph collects all the excess food in Egypt. Where does he store it?
In each city, where does the food that Joseph lays up come from?

cards.text: Joseph stores up grain in such abundance, like the sand of the sea. That's not a storehouse anymore, friend. That's a BEACH.

cards.question: Joseph keeps an exact count of all the grain he stores up.

cards.text: Before the years of famine arrive, Joseph and Asenath have two sons. I think that house just got a whole lot louder.

cards.question: Joseph names his firstborn son Manasseh. What does Joseph say God has made him do?
Joseph names his second son Ephraim, saying God has made him fruitful in the land of his fathers.
In Egypt, the seven years of ___ come to an end, and the seven years of ___ begin.

cards.text: It happens just as Joseph had said. And it's not only one place: there's famine in every country.

cards.question: There is famine in every country, but there is food throughout the land of ___.

cards.text: Then extreme hunger comes to all the land of Egypt, and the people cry out to Pharaoh for food. Every complaint in the whole kingdom, landing in ONE inbox.

cards.question: When the hungry people cry out to Pharaoh for food, what does he tell all the Egyptians?

answers.text: Go to Joseph and do whatever he tells you
Go to the priests and pray for the rain
Go to Canaan and buy your grain there

cards.text: The famine spreads over all the land, so Joseph opens up all the storehouses. Seven years of saving, and NOW those doors swing open.

cards.question: Joseph gives the grain away to the Egyptians for free.
The famine is severe over all the earth. Who comes to Joseph in Egypt to buy grain?

cards.text: And that's where we'll leave Joseph for now: storehouses open and the whole world at his door. Trust me, friend, this story is FAR from done.

findings.problem: Stop 1, card 4 quotes "Only with regard to the ___ will I be greater than you.", which isn't the exact BSB wording.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

findings.problem: The opening card states facts from before the passage: Joseph's interpretation of the dreams (Gen 41:25-32), his plan to store food (Gen 41:33-36) and his release from the dungeon (Gen 41:14). The card cites only Genesis 41:37 and gives no reference for those outside facts.

rule.text: Facts from outside the passage are fine when they help, like who a new person is or who wrote a letter, with their reference.

findings.problem: The joke 'when a whole room of officials agrees on something, you know it's a good plan' only restates the verse. It reads like a nice dad being pleasant, not a real laugh.

rule.text: If a line reads like a nice dad being pleasant, push it further.

findings.problem: 'A few verses ago this man was in a DUNGEON' is not accurate. Joseph is brought out of the dungeon in Gen 41:14, which is 25 verses earlier and outside this passage. The baker has not seen that verse in this lesson, and it has no reference.

rule.text: Noticing: What he points out must be true.

findings.problem: The statement opens with 'Pharaoh goes even bigger.' That wording signals True. Card 4 has also just said that only the throne is greater than Joseph and that all the people obey him. The baker has nothing to reason through.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: The wrong answer 'A palace' can be argued as right. In Gen 41:40 Pharaoh tells Joseph, 'You shall be in charge of my house.'

rule.text: No near-matches. A wrong answer never means the same as the right answer, or close to it. If a baker could argue it's right, replace it.

findings.problem: Card 14 asks about Gen 41:46. This card then goes back to Gen 41:45 ('Joseph took charge of all the land of Egypt'), so the walkthrough moves backward through the passage.

rule.text: Every story card moves the baker forward through the passage.

findings.problem: 'First day on the job and he's already out on the road' adds a time the text doesn't give. Gen 41:46 says only that Joseph left Pharaoh's presence and traveled throughout Egypt.

rule.text: Times stay true. No time in the text means none added.

findings.problem: Joseph's full reason for naming Manasseh is never told: God made him forget all his hardship 'and all my father's household' (Gen 41:51). This detail matters to the Joseph story, and the baker leaves Prep without it.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.

findings.problem: Earlier cards already give both blanks. Stop 2 card 1 says 'The seven years of abundance arrive.' Stop 2 card 6 says 'Before the years of famine arrive.' Stop 1 card 1 says 'seven years of famine.'

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.

findings.problem: The question's own setup says the famine 'is severe over all the earth,' and card 10 says there's 'famine in every country.' Together these rule out 'Only the Egyptians' and 'Only Pharaoh's officials.'

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: The 'story isn't over' line nearly copies the doc's example: 'And that's where we'll leave it for now. Trust me, friend, this story's not done.' It should be a new line written for this passage.

rule.text: The examples show the idea. Write your own line each time.
